name: M01 columns keyed by their count
why: [0,2] and [0,4] become one kind; they differ on a closer at indent 6 or 7, which no alphabet line has

name: M02 columns joined with no separator
why: [0,12] and [0,1,2] both join as 012; no pair of the alphabet columns collides

name: M03 columns keyed as nested or not
why: [0,2], [0,4], [0,3,6] become one kind

name: M04 columns keyed by the last one only
why: [0,3,6] and [0,6] become one kind; no pair of the alphabet columns shares a last column

name: M05 run length in a byte
why: a fence of 259 and a fence of 3 become one kind; no kind has a run over 5

name: M06 run length capped at 5
why: 6 and 7 backticks become one kind; no kind has a run over 5

name: M07 indent keyed by its length
why: one space and one tab become one kind (only '', two spaces and a tab are used, and their lengths differ)

name: M08 kind is the identity of the opener object
from: const kind = JSON.stringify([open.isCell, open.char, open.len, open.indent, open.columns]);
to: const kind = open as unknown as string;
why: structurally equal openers do not share a span: answer-equal, but only the timing rows on candidate objects can see the cost

name: M09 kind is the whole opener
from: const kind = JSON.stringify([open.isCell, open.char, open.len, open.indent, open.columns]);
why: the opener's own line number is in the key: same partition on the unit objects, none on computeRegions' candidates

name: M10 a one-line scan is not kept
to: if (k > from) lastScan.set(kind, { from, found, end: k });
why: cost only: the same question asked twice reads one line twice

name: M11 the longer span is kept
to: if (known === undefined || k > known.end) lastScan.set(kind, { from, found, end: k });
why: COST ONLY, out of order: the longer span is kept when a fresh scan starts before it. The product asks i + 1 for ascending i, so the case never arises; a descending sweep is quadratic in the cure itself (the performance lens), whichever span it keeps

name: M12 a hit narrows the span to the question
why: cost only for out-of-order questions

name: M13 the new span reaches back to the old one
to: { from: Math.min(from, known?.from ?? from), found, end: k }
why: a question in the gap between two spans is answered from the later

name: M14 one slot for every kind
to:
lastScan.clear();
    lastScan.set(kind, { from, found, end: k });
why: interleaved kinds rescan

name: M15 at most eight kinds kept
to:
if (lastScan.size >= 8) lastScan.clear();
    lastScan.set(kind, { from, found, end: k });
why: cost only: nine kinds interleaved in one run

name: M16 span end in 20 bits
why: a run past 2^20 lines

name: M17 span end in 24 bits
why: COST ONLY, past 2^24 lines: the span end is masked to 24 bits, never raised, so a span only shrinks and the answers stay right (`found` is not masked); a run of more than 16.7 million lines rescans. Argued, not run at that size (M16, 20 bits, is killed by the 1,100,000-line row)

name: M18 closer test before blank test
why: EQUIVALENT BEHAVIOUR: the closer is tested before the blank line, and a blank line is never a closer, so the answers are the same; one more read at each stop. The cost pins are relative (the whole sequence equals the first scan of each kind), so they allow it, as they allow reading lines[k] once (M19)

name: M19 each line read once
why: EQUIVALENT BEHAVIOUR: lines[k] is read once into a local: the same answers, half the reads of a line. The cost pins are relative, so they allow it (the first draft's 2(n-1) pin reddened it)

name: M20 blank test hand made, U+2005 missing
why: a line of U+2005 is not blank

name: M21 blank test by \s
why: EQUIVALENT: /^\s*$/ and trim() === "" agree on all 65,536 UTF-16 code units (the mutation lens), since \s is the WhiteSpace and LineTerminator set trim() strips

name: W01 asks two lines below the opener
why: a closer directly under a lone refused opener is not consumed

name: W02 asks with column zero only
why: a closer in a list item at indent 4 is code to this kind

name: W03 asks with run length 3
why: a three-run closer is taken for a four-run opener's

name: W04 asks with the backtick
why: a tilde opener looks for a backtick closer

name: W05 asks for an empty indent
why: an indented closer is not taken

name: W06 asks as a cell
why: a cell takes the exact run length only

name: W07 consumed > 0
why: EQUIVALENT: the call asks from i + 1 >= 1, so a found line is at least 1

name: W08 the map is shared between documents
from: const lastScan = new Map<string, { from: number; found: number; end: number }>();
to: const lastScan = ((globalThis as unknown as { __scan?: Map<string, { from: number; found: number; end: number }> }).__scan ??= new Map<string, { from: number; found: number; end: number }>());
why: spans of one document answer for the next

name: X1 isCloser not exported
from: export function isCloser(line: string, open: CloserShape)
why: the oracle test imports it

name: X2 makeConsumedCloserLine not exported
why: the tests import it
